headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a handful of popular IP‑lookup APIs that return **company / organization** data (and often contact details such as email, phone, or website).  
All of them expose a simple REST endpoint; you just need an API key (most offer a free tier).

| Service | Endpoint (example) | Free tier | Typical fields returned |
|---------|--------------------|-----------|------------------------|
| **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io/<IP>/json?token=<TOKEN>` | 50 000 req/month | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipstack.com** | `http://api.ipstack.com/<IP>?access_key=<KEY>&fields=company` | 10 000 req/month | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co/<IP>/json/?fields=company` | 1 000 req/day | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=<KEY>&ip=<IP>&fields=company` | 1 000 req/day | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipwhois.io** | `https://ipwhois.app/json/<IP>?fields=company` | 1 000 req/day | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/<IP>?api-key=<KEY>&fields=company` | 1 000 req/day | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |
| **ipqualityscore.com** | `https://www.ipqualityscore.com/api/json/company/<API_KEY>/<IP>` | 1 000 req/day | `company` (name, domain, industry, logo, phone, email, website) |

> **Tip:** Most of these services return the same set of fields under a `company` object.  
> Example response (ipinfo.io):

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "industry": "Internet",
    "logo": "https://ipinfo.io/static/img/logo.png",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com",
    "website": "https://www.google.com"
  },
  ...
}
```

### How to get started

1. **Sign up** for an account on one of the sites above.  
   *ipinfo.io* and *ipstack.com* are usually the easiest to start with because they have generous free tiers and clear documentation.

2. **Get your API key** (often called a “token” or “access key”).

3. **Make a request**.  
   Using `curl`:

   ```bash
   curl "https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN"
   ```

   Or in Python:

   ```python
   import requests
   resp = requests.get(
       "https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json",
       params={"token": "YOUR_TOKEN"}
   )
   data = resp.json()
   print(data["company"])
   ```

4. **Parse the `company` field** to extract the name, domain, phone, email, etc.

### Choosing the right provider

| Provider | Strengths | Caveats |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **ipinfo.io** | Very straightforward, includes logo URLs, free tier is generous. | Some fields (e.g., phone/email) may be missing for smaller companies. |
| **ipstack.com** | Offers a wide range of fields beyond company (city, timezone, etc.). | Free tier limited to 10 k/month; requires `fields=` param to avoid extra data. |
| **ipapi.co** | Simple, no extra cost for basic fields. | Free tier capped at 1 k/day; may throttle after that. |
| **ipgeolocation.io** | Good for bulk lookups, includes additional security fields. | Requires specifying `fields=` to keep payload small. |
| **ipwhois.io** | No signup needed for basic queries; great for quick tests. | Free tier limited to 1 k/day; may require upgrading for heavy use. |
| **ipdata.co** | Provides a rich set of fields, including ASN info. | Free tier limited to 1 k/day; requires API key. |
| **ipqualityscore.com** | Focuses on fraud detection; includes company data. | Free tier limited to 1 k/day; may be overkill if you only need company info. |

### Quick comparison of free tier limits

| Service | Requests per month | Notes |
|---------|--------------------|-------|
| ipinfo.io | 50 000 | Unlimited free tier for most developers. |
| ipstack.com | 10 000 | Good for moderate traffic. |
| ipapi.co | 30 000 | 1 000/day limit; 30 000/month if you stay below 1 k/day. |
| ipgeolocation.io | 30 000 | Same 1 k/day rule. |
| ipwhois.io | 30 000 | Same 1 k/day rule. |
| ipdata.co | 30 000 | Same 1 k/day rule. |
| ipqualityscore.com | 30 000 | Same 1 k/day rule. |

> **Pro tip:** If you’re building a production system, consider caching the results (e.g., Redis or a local DB) so you don’t hit the API for every lookup.

---

#### Bottom line

For a quick, reliable API that returns company data with contact info, **ipinfo.io** is usually the best starting point. If you need more fields or a different pricing model, try **ipstack.com** or **ipapi.co**. All of them expose a simple GET endpoint and return the company data in a consistent JSON structure. Happy coding!
